concerns.text: Tasks T095, T096, T097, and T098 in Phase 7 are marked as [P] (parallel-safe) and depend on artifacts from Phase 3/4 (T013d, T020b, T022). However, Phase 8 explicitly lists these exact tasks as 'REMOVED' due to scope creep. This creates a semantic contradiction where the task list orders work that the project scope has already rejected, violating the 'Producer before consumer' and 'Foundational tasks first' principles by including non-existent dependencies.

Task T020a (Subset Selection) depends on T013d (Geometry Export) to filter molecules with valid optimized geometries. However, T020a is marked [P] (parallel-safe) in the list, but the description explicitly states it 'MUST run AFTER T013d' to ensure stratification is based on valid geometries. If T020a runs in parallel with T013d, it will fail to find the required input files, violating the 'Producer before consumer' dependency rule.

Task T021 (Train Models) depends on T020b (DFT Calculation) and T020c (Split Generation). T020b depends on T013d (Geometry Export). The task list marks T021 as [P] (parallel-safe), but it cannot run until T020b and T020c complete. Marking a task as [P] when it has hard sequential dependencies on other tasks in the same phase is a semantic violation of the parallel-safe tag.

Task T004c (Normalize Dataset Filename) is marked as incomplete [ ] and depends on T004b. However, T010 (Validate Data) and T011 (Confounds Analysis) are marked as complete [X] but depend on T004c's output (`data/raw/barrier_dataset.csv`). This implies a logical ordering violation where consumers are marked complete before their producer is complete.
